name: Janitri
tagline: Wireless monitors for pregnancy and labour care
excerpt: Janitri, which makes fetal and maternal monitoring devices, chose Namita Thapar as its solo investor on Shark Tank India Season 2.
content:
Janitri builds medical-grade devices that track a baby's heart rate, the mother's heart rate and contractions during pregnancy and labour, for use in hospitals and at home. Its founder, Arun Agarwal, is from Alwar in Rajasthan.

The company pitched in Shark Tank India Season 2, Episode 12. Peyush Bansal and Amit Jain made a joint offer, but Namita Thapar, whose family runs the drugmaker Emcure, pushed for a solo deal. Business Today reported that she put in ₹1 crore for a 2.5% stake. Months later, Thapar wrote on LinkedIn that Janitri's monthly sales had grown from about ₹10 lakh to about ₹50 lakh, as Business Today reported.

In May 2023, Outlook Startup reported a $1.1 million pre-Series A round led by India Accelerator, with Thapar among the participants. Audited revenue and valuation have not been reported in the outlets we track.

The pitch shows the value of a sector expert: the founder picked the shark with the most healthcare experience over a joint offer from two others.

shark_tank.pitch_summary: Arun Agarwal pitched Janitri's pregnancy and labour monitors and asked ₹1 crore for 2.5%. He turned down a joint offer from Peyush Bansal and Amit Jain and took Namita Thapar's solo deal.

faq.q: Did Janitri get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. Namita Thapar invested ₹1 crore for 2.5% in Season 2, Episode 12.

faq.q: Why did Janitri choose Namita Thapar?
faq.a: The founder preferred her healthcare background over a joint offer from Peyush Bansal and Amit Jain.
Audited revenue has not been reported in the outlets we track.

faq.q: Has Janitri raised money since the show?
faq.a: Yes. Outlook Startup reported a $1.1 million pre-Series A round in May 2023.

lessons: In regulated sectors such as medical devices, an investor's industry network can matter more than the cheque.
Two sharks bidding together does not always beat one specialist.
Monthly sales figures quoted by an investor are a claim, not a filing; wait for audited numbers.
notes: Ask ₹1 cr for 2.5% sourced to India.com (Zee Media news site), not a top-tier outlet. Wikipedia lists a condition (extra 2.5% if ₹20 cr revenue missed next year); no credible outlet confirms it, so it is left out. A June 2025 $1.4M round led by Ashish Kacholia was reported only by aggregators; left out. City not sourced.
